title: Constant derived mapping sheaves of bounded finite complexes
statement: Let $U$ be a scheme with its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $B$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $E,G$ be bounded cochain complexes of $B$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], each term a finite set. Write $\underline E,\underline G$ for their termwise constant sheaf complexes [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. The sheafifications [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the derived Hom and Isom presheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-derived-map-presheaves] between $\underline E,\underline G$ are isomorphic respectively to the constant sheaves with values $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$ and $\operatorname{Isom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$. The latter value may be empty.

source.place: Tags 094G lemma-locally-constant, 09BE lemma-locally-constant-map, and 08FR lemma-local-actual; Constant derived mapping sheaves of bounded finite complexes

proof.text: For bounded finite algebraic E,G choose a bounded-above finite free resolution P of E. The finite-cone hypothesis holds: a finite free complex and E have finite terms, so every mapping cone has finite cohomology.

With $P\to E$ as above, let $N$ be an upper bound on the terms of $P$, and choose $e,g$ such that $E^i=0$ for $i<e$ and $G^i=0$ for $i<g$ and $m\leq\min(e,g-2)$. Let $F=\sigma_{\geq m}P$: it has the terms $P^i$ for $m\leq i\leq N$, and zero elsewhere. It is bounded finite free. The inclusion into $P$ is an isomorphism on cohomology for $i>m$ and surjective for $i=m$, directly from cycles modulo boundaries. Compose with $P\to E$ and take its cone $C$. The long exact sequence gives $H^i(C)=0$ for $i\geq m$. Orthogonality gives $\operatorname{Hom}(C,G)=\operatorname{Hom}(C[-1],G)=0$, because $C\in D^{\leq m-1}$ and $C[-1]\in D^{\leq m}$ while $G\in D^{\geq g}$. Exactness of Hom out of the cone triangle, and its rotations, now identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(F,G)$ by precomposition.

source.place: Tag 09BE, lemma-locally-constant-map: agent extension using a bounded finite-free approximation; cone calculation as in Tag 064U

proof.text: All terms of $F,E,C$ are finite. Apply exactness of constant finite-module sequences to the cycles, boundaries and cohomology sequences of $C$. It gives $H^i(\underline C)=\underline{H^i(C)}$. Termwise constant sheaves commute with the finite direct sums, differentials and signs in the cone. Thus the constant cone lies in $D^{\leq m-1}$ on every localized etale site, while $\underline G$ lies in $D^{\geq g}$. The same orthogonality and Hom-out-of-triangle exactness as in the algebraic truncation argument give $\operatorname{Hom}(\underline E,\underline G)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\underline F,\underline G)$ on every etale object. These bijections commute with restriction: they are all precomposition by the restriction of the single fixed map $\underline F\to\underline E$. Here constant complexes and restrictions are those in the constant-complex and derived-map-presheaf definitions.

source.place: Tag 09BE, lemma-locally-constant-map, finite-source extension; exact constant sequences from etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03RX

proof.text: Let $H=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(F,G)$. Since each finite free $B$-module is projective (lift the images of its basis along any surjection), the bounded-projective derived-map-representative theorem identifies $H$ with chain maps $F\to G$ modulo homotopy. Taking constant complexes gives a natural map from the constant presheaf $H$ to the derived Hom presheaf of $\underline F,\underline G$. It is locally surjective: local-actual (1) represents every derived morphism by a chain map after a cover. Apply the constant-sheaf morphism lemma to its finitely many components. On a common refinement every component is induced by a $B$-linear map $F^i\to G^i$. On a nonempty member, taking any geometric stalk turns the chain equations into the same equations for these module maps, by the constant-stalk identification. They therefore form a chain map $F\to G$, and its class in $H$ induces the original local derived morphism. Empty members contribute no sections to check.

source.place: Tag 08FR, lemma-local-actual (1); Tag 09BE, lemma-locally-constant-map, and sites-modules.tex Tag 093S

proof.text: For local injectivity, take two algebraic chain maps whose images agree in actual derived Hom on an etale object. Their difference becomes null-homotopic after a cover by local-actual (2). There are finitely many homotopy components $h^i:\underline F^i\to\underline G^{i-1}$. The constant-sheaf morphism lemma makes them module maps on a common refinement. A geometric stalk on any nonempty member turns $\alpha^i=d_G^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}d_F^i$ into an algebraic homotopy, so the two classes in $H$ agree. If their images agree only in sheafified Hom, the site sheafification-sections lemma first makes the equality actual after a cover. This proves local injectivity in that case as well. Together with the local chain representative argument and that lemma, the induced map of sheafifications is bijective: locally represent a target section, lift it by the local chain representative argument, and glue the lifts; on overlaps local injectivity makes their images agree in the source sheaf. Uniqueness follows in the same way. The set $H$ is finite since there are finitely many degreewise maps $F^i\to G^i$ and only finitely many nonzero degrees. The algebraic and localized truncation comparisons identify this constant Hom sheaf with the constant finite set $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$. This proves the constant-complex Hom comparison.

source.place: Tag 08FR, lemma-local-actual (2); sites.tex Tags 00WB/00WK, theorem-plus and lemma-sections-sheafification; finite Hom calculation

proof.text: Under the Hom-sheaf identification, the sheafification of the isomorphism presheaf is the constant subset $\operatorname{Isom}_{D(B)}(E,G)$. Indeed an algebraic isomorphism and its inverse give inverse constant derived maps. Conversely, if a constant algebraic map represents an actual derived isomorphism on a nonempty etale object, an exact geometric stalk functor takes its inverse to an inverse in $D(B)$, so the map was an algebraic isomorphism. A germ coming from a sheafified isomorphism can be represented by an actual isomorphism after a cover by the site sheafification-sections lemma. Equalities with the local constant Hom representative can be made actual after a further cover, so the preceding test applies to germs as well. On overlaps the algebraic isomorphism representatives agree after refinement by the local injectivity proved for Hom; the same site-sections lemma then glues them to the constant isomorphism sheaf, with uniqueness. Hence the isomorphism sheaf is finite locally constant; its value is the empty set when the two model objects are not isomorphic. Exactness and the constant-stalk theorem are used on underlying abelian groups, and their naturality with multiplication by every $b\in B$ makes the same maps $B$-linear.

theorem finiteRing_constant_derived_mapping_sheaves
    (U : Scheme.{u}) (B : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing B] [Finite B]
    (E G : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) ℤ)
    (hE : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (E.X n))
    (hG : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (G.X n))
    (hEfin : ∀ n : ℤ, Finite (E.X n)) (hGfin : ∀ n : ℤ, Finite (G.X n)) :
    Nonempty
      (((presheafToSheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).obj
        (derivedHomPresheaf B
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            (((constantSheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B)).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj E))
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            (((constantSheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B)).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj G)))) ≅
        (constantSheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj G)) ∧
    Nonempty
      (((presheafToSheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).obj
        (derivedIsoPresheaf B
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            (((constantSheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B)).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj E))
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            (((constantSheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B)).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj G)))) ≅
        (constantSheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj G))
